patches.old: To justify the dimension monotonicity being used, pull back any δ-cover of F under φ. Its preimages cover I, and every preimage has diameter at most that of the corresponding covering member: distances of preimage points equal distances of their images. Empty preimages contribute zero. Thus Hscale(a,δ,I)≤Hscale(a,δ,F) for all a>0 and δ>0, and taking suprema gives Hmeasure(a,I)≤Hmeasure(a,F).
patches.new: To justify the dimension monotonicity being used, fix b>0, δ_2>0 and any countable δ_2-cover Q of F. Define Qpre_i={t∈I:φ(t)∈Q_i}. These preimages cover I, and diam Qpre_i≤diam Q_i because distances of preimage points equal distances of their images. Empty preimages contribute zero. Hence Hscale(b,δ_2,I) is at most the b-cost of Q. Taking the infimum over all Q proves Hscale(b,δ_2,I)≤Hscale(b,δ_2,F) for every b>0,δ_2>0, and taking suprema gives Hmeasure(b,I)≤Hmeasure(b,F) for all b>0. Close these cover, scale and exponent quantifiers.
